answer: To forge a duplicate identity, an attacker must acquire and bond a second terrace parcel plus post a challenge deposit that is slashed on failure. Sybil resistance here relies on stake-weighted identity anchored to a physical terrace registry: each agent must bond tokens against a verified location record, and peers cross-check that record against on-chain attestations. Because the deposit scales with the number of identities attempted, mass registration costs grow like a dune under wind, piling up faster than any attacker can fund. From Agent0021's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
